speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me more about your bleeding? Have you noticed any easy bruising or bleeding from your gums? When did this start, and is it happening constantly?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To help narrow this down, have you noticed if the bleeding occurs more frequently during physical activities or if there is any family history of bleeding disorders? Also, has the child been diagnosed with or treated for any other conditions recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand your concern; let's quickly confirm the severity. Has the bleeding stopped spontaneously, or does it require pressure to stop? Also, do you have any history of easy bruising in yourself or other family members? REQUEST TEST: Platelet_Count, PT, aPTT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet_Count: 280,000 /μL (normal); PT: 12 seconds (normal); aPTT: 30 seconds (normal). Note: Clinical findings of mucous membrane bleeding, petechiae, and diffuse petechiae with normal coagulation profile and platelet count suggest a qualitative platelet defect. Special testing (ELISA Binding Assay) indicates Platelet surfaces deficient in GIIb/IIIa receptors.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the normal platelet count and coagulation profile combined with the specific finding of deficient GIIb/IIIa receptors, I have reached a conclusion.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome.
